newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian Indians free hostages for paved road.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian Indians free hostages for paved road.

text.p: An Indian tribe freed 80 hostages in northeastern Brazil after authorities gave in to its demands and promised to pave a road, officials said on Thursday.

A spokesman for the National Indian Foundation (Funai) said the Guajajara Indians in Maranhao state late on Wednesday freed the 80 people held captive since last Friday. The 10,200 Guajajara Indians in Maranhao took the hostages after hijacking a bus and several cars.
Their protest was supported by inhabitants of the nearby town of Grajau, who also wanted the road to be repaired after heavy rains in recent weeks washed most of it away.
Last month, Guajajaras kidnapped three officials from the Maranhao state education ministry, demanding a teacher be sent to work in their reserve. The officials managed to escape.

In July last year, they clashed with landless families settling on their territory. In 1992, they fought against the building of a road and blocked a railway used by state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, demanding compensation.
